issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: 'Risky Behavior' is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which is dominated by high threat perception, safety behaviors, severe hopelessness, and a robbery-related fear structure. A patient who is persistently choosing safe seats and feeling intensely endangered would more plausibly show avoidance/hypervigilance than generalized risk-taking; this reads as an opposing clinical state within the Threat node.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Authority Figures: Being around people in authority or uniform
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Authority Figures' is a weak fit for mugging/robbery trauma in this profile. There is no supporting trigger, memory, or appraisal content involving police, security staff, uniforms, or institutional betrayal, so this strategy targets a symptom context not otherwise represented in the formulation. For this trauma type, avoiding authority/uniformed people is not impossible, but here it lacks clinical linkage and appears incoherent with the rest of the selected items.

vignette: Linh is a 44-year-old South Eastern Asian male who works as a nurse at a local hospital. He has been married for over two decades and had always prided himself on his resilience and dedication to helping others. However, his life took a sudden and harrowing turn when he was mugged while walking home from work late one night. The incident unfolded swiftly and brutally. As Linh turned the corner onto his street, a masked assailant appeared out of the shadows, brandishing a knife. The shock and terror were overwhelming as he tried to fend off the attacker but ended up sustaining deep cuts on his arm and leg. The assault lasted only minutes, but the trauma lingered long after Linh managed to escape and call for help. In the weeks following the mugging, Linh found himself constantly scanning his environment for any signs of potential threats. He would keep checking mirrors in public places, feeling an almost compulsive need to ensure no one was lurking behind him. This behavior extended even into his workplace where he would often distract himself with work tasks just to avoid thinking about the attack. The memories of that night were vivid and painful, as though he could see every detail as if looking at photographs. Each time a memory surfaced, Linh felt the same physical pain in his injured limbs. The clarity of these visual memories made it impossible for him to escape the trauma. He would often wake up in the middle of the night drenched in sweat, unable to fall back asleep. Linh’s fear was not just confined to the past; he began experiencing intense anxiety about the future as well. He became hyper-aware of his surroundings at all times and always chose seating arrangements that allowed him a clear view of any exits or potential threats. This behavior extended to social settings where he would avoid going out alone, fearing another attack. Over time, Linh’s maladaptive strategies began to take a toll on both his personal and professional life. At work, his constant scanning and distraction affected his concentration and interactions with patients. He often felt like he was losing touch with the empathy that had always driven him as a nurse. His wife noticed these changes too; they started having frequent arguments because Linh would avoid going out together or even leaving the house. The psychological burden also grew heavier. Linh began to believe there was something inherently wrong with him, which made the event happen. This led to an overwhelming sense of hopelessness and a belief that nothing good could ever happen to him again. He became increasingly isolated, both from his colleagues at work and family members at home. What finally brought Linh to seek help was a realization that he was no longer living but merely surviving. The fear of another attack, combined with the relentless memories and physical pain, had taken over his life. Despite his fears, Linh hoped therapy could provide him some relief from these overwhelming thoughts and sensations. He was most afraid of being trapped in this state forever, unable to recover or enjoy life again. Linh’s journey towards healing is complex but grounded in a deep desire for peace and a sense of safety. His clinical portrait reveals the intricate interplay between his traumatic experience and the symptoms he now endures, all stemming from that single night that changed everything.
